question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(3),$ calculate $P(X\le \frac{1}{3}\,|\,X>\frac{1}{4}).$
question.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =3,$ $s=\frac{1}{4},$ and $s+t=\frac{1}{3}.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{12}
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le \frac{1}{3}\,|\,X>\frac{1}{4}) & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(3)\cdot (1/12)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-1/4}\end{aligned}
$$
